Every declaration that calls `getOrderTypes` in the REST module, best first:

1. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/OrderTypeResource1_10.java` lines 120–123, `doGetAll`: direct call with `includeAll`, backs the `/ws/rest/v1/ordertype` list.
2. The same file, lines 128–139, `doSearch`: direct call with `includeAll`, then filters by `q`. Backs `/ws/rest/v1/ordertype?q=`.
3. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/OrderableResource1_10.java` lines 64–123, `search`: calls `getOrderTypes(false)` on line 69 and uses the result to resolve order types and concept classes. Backs `/ws/rest/v1/orderable`.
4. The same file, line 134, `getOrderableConceptClasses`: takes the list that `search` built from `getOrderTypes`, so it is affected indirectly. Only the declaration line was checked.
5. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_10/OrderTypeController1_10Test.java` lines 94–100: test that compares the list endpoint's size with `getOrderTypes(true)`. Test code, not a resource.
6. The same test file, lines 111–132: search test that depends on the `q` filter results.
7. The same test file, lines 144–158: create test that counts order types before and after a POST.

Outside the REST module, core's `OrderServiceImpl.getOrderTypesByClassName` also calls it, but that is not a `/ws/rest/v1` resource, so I left it out. I used four of the ten search calls and six of the twenty read calls.
